content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain waffles are a ready‑to‑cook frozen product made from whole wheat, oat or rye grains. They contain more fiber and nutrients than traditional waffles made with refined flour and retain the natural taste of the grain.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole grain waffles are typically produced without artificial colors or flavors.
Freezing preserves most B‑vitamins and minerals found in whole grains.
They can be quickly prepared in a toaster or oven, making them a convenient breakfast or snack option.
Whole grains are considered healthier because they keep the bran and germ intact.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: The whole grains provide dietary fiber that supports digestive health and promotes satiety.

items.title: Contains complex carbohydrates
items.content: Complex carbs release energy slowly, helping maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Waffles contain thiamine, riboflavin, niacin and folate, which are essential for metabolism.

items.title: Provides minerals
items.content: They supply magnesium, iron and zinc, important for muscle function and immunity.

items.title: Low in trans fats
items.content: When produced correctly, whole grain waffles contain little to no trans fats, making them heart‑friendlier.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The product contains wheat, so it is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some varieties may have added salt; those monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: While less calorie‑dense than white‑flour waffles, they still provide a notable amount of energy and can contribute to weight gain if over‑consumed.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Toast the frozen waffles in a toaster, oven or microwave until golden and crisp. Serve with berries, yogurt, nut butter or a drizzle of honey. They can also be cubed and added to salads or soups for extra crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the waffles in the freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. After thawing, use within 2–3 days and store in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
